summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, type 1 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for acute respiratory failure requiring intubation. She presented with severe pulmonary edema and hypercarbia, initially managed with BiPAP but progressed to mechanical ventilation. During her ICU stay, she underwent cardiac catheterization revealing coronary artery disease, with a stent placed in the LAD. She developed cardiogenic shock and acute kidney injury requiring initiation of dialysis. Coagulase-negative staph bacteremia was identified, treated with vancomycin without line removal due to the tunnelled dialysis catheter. A yeast urinary tract infection was treated with fluconazole. She had transient atrial fibrillation and vocal cord paralysis post-extubation, managed conservatively. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted, and she was transitioned to outpatient dialysis. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs and a plan for close follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Acute kidney failure with lesion of tubular necrosis
Subendocardial infarction, initial episode of care
Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx, unspecified
